original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points}
Let $R$ be a ring.
Assume that $R$ has finitely many minimal primes
$\mathfrak q_1, \ldots, \mathfrak q_t$, and that
$\mathfrak q_1 \cup \ldots \cup \mathfrak q_t$ is the set
of zerodivisors of $R$.
Then the total ring of fractions $Q(R)$ is equal to
$R_{\mathfrak q_1} \times \ldots \times R_{\mathfrak q_t}$.

semantic_review_note: The total ring of fractions Q(R) decomposes as a product of localizations at the finitely many minimal primes when their union is precisely the set of zerodivisors. The proposed statement retains both the finiteness and zerodivisor assumptions, as well as all factors R_{q_i}.
